cefrAlignment: Now fits B2 (CEFR CV reading for information and argument: can understand articles in which writers adopt particular viewpoints and can identify the content and relevance of detailed information): both passages are now 350–365 words (they were 206 and 146, below the B2 range), with hedged claims, qualifiers and a stated authorial stance.
examFidelity: TFNG and YNNG follow IELTS conventions (False must contradict, Not Given must be absent, statements in passage order, YNNG for writer's views); both exam tags are now practised, and the answer-wording tip no longer contains the confusing 'Write T, F or NG'.
fixes: Fixed an ambiguous model item: 'Paris was the first city to introduce bike-sharing' was keyed False against 'one of the first large-scale schemes', which does not contradict it. The passage now states Copenhagen's 1995 coin-operated scheme (verified), so False is clear, and the walkthrough explains why 'one of the first' alone would not be enough
Corrected the four-step method, which said a changed qualifier usually means False; this contradicted ex3 q1 (many vs most = Not Given). It now teaches checking for real contradiction
Replaced the learn example 'The museum is more than twenty years old → True', which depended on today's date (outside knowledge), with 'opened in the late 1990s'
Reordered ex1 statements to follow passage order (fuel prices came after Copenhagen although it comes first in the text)
Reworded the Copenhagen statement so its contradiction with 'never fully abandoned cycling' is exact
Extended the bike passage with a fifth paragraph (e-bikes) and added two items (one F, one NG word-matching trap); softened 'Researchers now agree' to 'Many transport researchers now argue'
Rewrote the work-from-home passage as an argumentative text and turned ex2 into a Yes/No/Not Given exercise (6 statements, 2 Y / 2 N / 2 NG), so the YNNG tag and tip are now practised
Added a missing explanation to ex3 q3 and a new ex3 item on when to use YNNG versus TFNG
Updated the definition of False to 'contradicts', and updated the objectives, key points and the IELTS answer-wording tip
openConcerns: Because this file is the reference lesson named in CONTENT_GUIDE.md, a human should confirm that the larger restructure (ex2 is now YNNG) is acceptable as the template for other lessons.
learnerOutcome: A learner can reliably tell False from Not Given by checking for real contradiction, handle qualifiers such as all, most, several and the first, and apply the same method to Yes/No/Not Given questions about a writer's views.
